Tapoloka
------------------------------------------
This is one of the six lokas or worlds above the भूलोक or the earth. It is the sixth, calculated from भूलोक as the first.
According to the Viṣṇupurāṇa (2.7), the पितृस् (manes) called Vairājas live here.
The Bhāgavata (2.5.39) declares that devotees of कृष्ण who please him by great austerities attain this world.
The Vyāsabhāṣya on the Yogasūtras (3.26) of पतञ्जलि (200 B. C.) describes it as the abode of certain divine beings—Ābhāsvaras, Mahābhāsvaras and सत्त्व-mahābhāsvaras—who have a very long life, who are ever immersed in meditation and whose knowledge is immense.

tapas
(‘that which causes suffering’)
------------------------------------------
The word तपस् comes from the root-verb ‘tap’ (santāpe, in the sense of suffering). Hence it means any discipline that causes suffering to the body-मिन्द् complex.
We find the word used even in the Ṛgveda (10.154.2). There, it is interpreted as penances like कृच्छ्र and meditation on हिरण्यगर्भ. (See KṚCCHARA and HIRAṆYAGARBHA for details.)
It is also used in the उपनिषद्स् like the Chāndogya (5.10.1, 2) and the Muṇḍaka (

) in the sense of performance of one’s duties and austerities.
Dharmasūtras like those of गौतम (19.15) equate it with a number of observances like ब्रह्मचर्य (celibacy), satyavacana (speaking the truth), ārdra-vastratā (wearing wet clothes on the body until they dry up), adhaśśāyitā (sleeping on the bare ground), अहिṁसा (non-injury) and astainya (not depriving anyone of his possessions) and so on. The duration for the observance of these as expiations varies from a year up to one day, depending on the nature of sin.
The Yogasūtras of पतञ्जलि (200 B. C.) (2.1; 2.32) uses the word in the sense of control over ड़ोओद्, forbearance as also the performance of कृच्छ्र and चान्द्रायण. (See CĀNDRĀYAṆA and KṚCCHRA.)
The Bhagavadgītā (17.14-19) deals with तपस् from three angles: śārīra (physical), vāṅmaya (as pertaining to speech) and mānasa (mental). Honouring and serving gods and holy persons, cleanli-ness, celibacy and non-violence belong to the first category. Sweet but truthful speech belongs to the second category. Control of मिन्द् and purity of emotions are the essential elements of the third.
The Gītā further qualifies these three kinds from the standpoint of the three guṇas. Sāttvik तपस् is that which is performed by persons of pure character possessing concentration and faith. The तपस् performed by persons who are hypocrites, for selfish benefits like name and honour, is termed rājasik. The one undertaken by foolish persons to harm others is classed at tāmasik.

taptakṛcchra
------------------------------------------
This is one of the expiatory rites. It may be spread over two days, four days or twelve days or even twenty-one days, depending on the nature of the sin committed.
Hot water, hot milk and hot ghee (of prescribed quantity and once in a day) are to be taken during the first three periods, the last being spent in ड़स्तिन्ग्.
